leads.title: Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms - Section 15(1)
leads.documents: Constitutional equality guarantee interpreted to protect LGBTQ people from discrimination based on sexual orientation; applies to all laws and government institutions including law enforcement in Yukon; basis for Yukon rights machinery.
leads.detail: Quoted in text as s.15(1) equality provision; Charter included in Constitution in 1982, came into force 1985. No URL visible in provided text.

leads.title: Egan v. Canada, 1995 - Supreme Court of Canada
leads.documents: Landmark ruling that sexual orientation is included in Section 15 as analogous ground; establishes constitutional protection applicable in Yukon.
leads.detail: Cited as 'Egan v Canada' 1995 landmark decision. No URL visible in provided text.

leads.title: Vriend v Alberta, 1998 - Supreme Court of Canada
leads.documents: Held failure to include sexual orientation in human rights law violates Section 15; led to rule that as of 2017 all provinces, territories (including Yukon) and federal government explicitly include sexual orientation and gender identity as prohibited grounds.
leads.detail: Cited as 'Vriend v Alberta' 1998 decision. No URL visible in provided text.

leads.title: Civil Marriage Act (2005) - Federal Parliament
leads.documents: Legalized same-sex marriage nationwide in Canada including Yukon; Yukon was among jurisdictions recognizing same-sex marriage by July 2005; confirms relationship recognition status for visitors/residents in Yukon.
leads.detail: Cited as federal Civil Marriage Act passed July 20, 2005; Supreme Court reference December 2004 upheld it. No URL visible.

leads.title: Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1968-69 (Bill C-150)
leads.documents: Decriminalized same-sex sexual activity in private between consenting adults in Canada including Yukon; brought into force June 27, 1969 upon royal assent.
leads.detail: Cited as 'Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1968-69 (also known as Bill C-150)'. No URL visible.

leads.title: Bill C-75 (incorporating Bill C-32) - Repeal of Criminal Code Section 159
leads.documents: Repealed archaic anal intercourse offence; set equal age of consent at 16 (18 with trust/authority/dependency); received royal assent June 21, 2019; documents current criminal legal status and enforcement baseline in Yukon.
leads.detail: Cited as Bill C-32 introduced Nov 15, 2016, incorporated into Bill C-75 tabled late March 2018, enacted June 21, 2019. Statement by MP Randy Boissonnault quoted. No URL visible.

leads.title: Canadian Human Rights Act + Provincial/Territorial Human Rights Acts
leads.documents: Federal Act covers federal government and federally regulated workplaces; Yukon/territorial human rights laws cover schools, rental housing, health care, most workplaces; article states discrimination on sexual orientation and gender identity or expression now prohibited by all provinces and territories and federal government.
leads.detail: Cited as 'The Canadian Human Rights Act is of relatively limited application' vs provincial laws. No URL visible.

leads.title: Expungement of Historically Unjust Convictions Act
leads.documents: Allows persons convicted of pre-1969 homosexual acts or under repealed s.159 to have RCMP/federal and notified provincial/municipal records destroyed/removed; documents remedial rights machinery.
leads.detail: Cited with French title 'Loi sur la radiation de condamnations constituant des injustices historiques', royal assent June 21, 2018; Parole Board distinction expungement vs pardon quoted. No URL visible.

leads.title: Yukon same-sex adoption legalization (2003)
leads.documents: Documents Yukon-specific family/parental rights status: adoption by same-sex couples legalized in Yukon in 2003 as part of nationwide rollout.
leads.detail: Cited in list: 'Northwest Territories (2002) and Yukon (2003)'. No statute name or URL visible in provided text.

leads.title: Federal Court Challenges Program (1985 expansion)
leads.documents: Government funding mechanism that funded Section 15 equality test cases advancing LGBTQ rights; documents enforcement/access-to-justice machinery applicable to Yukon claims.
leads.detail: Cited as expanded in 1985 to fund test cases challenging federal legislation re Charter equality rights. No URL visible.
